cases.title: Profitable, cheap, but the market is going away
reasons: Step 1 (kill criteria): none met. Net debt/EBITDA is 0.4x, well under the 4x limit. There is no controlling shareholder (insiders 4%, top holder Vanguard 9%), and the facts report no regulatory issue.

Step 3 (fit): two judgment criteria are not met. (a) Segment: rapid antigen tests for respiratory viruses are in-vitro diagnostics, but they are a disposable point-of-care product line. They are not instruments, assays, OEM analyzers or lab automation as the thesis lists them. This is borderline, since an antigen test is technically an assay, but the business is pandemic-driven testing volume rather than the platform segments we like. (b) Why the price is low: the 62% fall over 12 months is not temporary. Revenue has fallen for three consecutive years as pandemic-era testing volumes disappear, and the latest release shows a further 30% decline. Management has no new product with meaningful sales, so there is no product-transition recovery to wait for. The thesis calls this a structural loss of market, and it is not a product transition, destocking or a one-off charge. Margins stay positive (24% EBITDA) only because of cost cuts, which does not offset shrinking revenue.

Flags (no effect on the verdict): no holder is above the 25% flag threshold. Vanguard holds 9% and insiders hold 4%. Recurring revenue (consumables, service) is unconfirmed. Test sales may be largely one-off, which would be a warning only.

Conclusion: this is not a Reject, because no listed kill criterion is met. It is not a Priority, because the price drop looks structural. The verdict is Radar for failing the 'why the price is low' criterion.
